basis: Benign sweat-gland neoplasm arising in the dermis.
Desmin-related skeletal myopathy with defining cardiomyopathy and conduction disease. Respiratory failure reflects respiratory muscle weakness.
Lysosomal storage with neurodegeneration; skeletal abnormalities in 30-99%, retinal disease/visual impairment roughly half. Hepatosplenomegaly alone does not establish dysfunction.
Sparse syndrome record describes seizures, hemiparesis, hemiatrophy and skeletal abnormalities, supporting neurologic and structural musculoskeletal disease.
Antibody immunodeficiency; bronchiectasis documents chronic airway damage in 2/2 patients. Autoimmune thrombocytopenia is a separately diagnosed disease.
Lesion of the plantar peripheral nerve.
Disordered glucagon secretion is an endocrine pancreas disorder.
Autoimmune superficial blistering skin disease. Oral involvement is uncommon, below 30%.
Congenital cerebellar hypoplasia or aplasia defines Chiari type IV.
Alpha-1-antitrypsin Pittsburgh causes a coagulation inhibitor defect and bleeding; it does not imply conventional antitrypsin-deficiency liver or lung disease.
Genetically defined combined immunodeficiency; no common additional organ damage is established in the record.
Definition specifies an undifferentiated embryonal sarcoma originating in the liver.
Malignant precursor T-cell neoplasm; lymphoma also requires the infectious_immune mechanism axis. Mediastinal location alone does not establish lung damage.
Focal aneurysmal abnormality of retinal capillaries, involving the eye and its blood vessels.
Cerebral edema and encephalopathy define PRES. Visual symptoms arise centrally; associated hypertension does not establish an additional affected organ.
Structural loss of functional small intestine causes intestinal failure and malabsorption. Treatment-associated liver disease is excluded.
Lipoprotein disorder defined by intestinal malabsorption and neurologic disease; retinal degeneration/visual loss in 30-79%. Anemia in 30-79% omitted under cap; hepatic damage uncommon.
Selective IgA antibody deficiency. Recurrent respiratory and intestinal infections do not establish common persistent organ damage.
Patau syndrome features major brain, heart and skeletal malformations; microphthalmia/ocular malformations occur in roughly half. Renal and oral malformations omitted under cap.
Methionine-cycle disorder with encephalopathy and liver dysfunction; muscle atrophy 2/2, raised CK 3/6. Cardiac defects and hearing loss, each at least 2/6, omitted under cap.
Umbrella neoplasm of lymphocytic and plasma cells. Lymphoma-specific immune labeling and subtype-specific organ infiltration do not apply across the entire group.
Congenital hypomyelinating peripheral neuropathy; weakness and secondary muscle wasting do not establish a primary muscle lesion.
Defined by arrhythmogenic cardiomyopathy, palmoplantar keratoderma and woolly hair. Vertigo does not establish vestibular damage; cleft lip is not an established common feature.
Craniosynostosis and limb malformations define the syndrome; ptosis 80-99% and airway cartilaginous sleeve 20/20 support eye and airway involvement. Neurologic damage varies by subtype.
Usually cutaneous melanoma; distant metastatic disease commonly occupies lung (~40-70%), liver (~30-50%) and brain (~30-50%) over its course. Frequencies vary with metastatic stage.
